style: 3D animated (Pixar-style CG) for 0-57.13 s; hard cut to an 11-shot live-action handheld phone 'real me' lifestyle tag 57.13-59.84 s. Single-word white captions (bold condensed caps, black outline) at lower-middle; small white hook title 'MOM SAID I'D FAIL' + skull emoji in the first second.
logline: A teen spends his savings on hoodies to resell; his mom calls it a waste and tells him to focus on school. He grinds through a month of listing and packing, the orders explode, Mom ends up packing beside him - and then finds out he has already bought a closet full of more stock.

hook.mechanic: Doubter confrontation cold open: on-screen title 'MOM SAID I'D FAIL' over Mom bursting through the door mid-shout ('What is all this inventory?'), cut to a wide showing walls of stacked stock, and a humiliating answer ('How many have you sold?' - 'Two.') - stakes, villain-of-the-moment and the promised payback are all set in 7 s.
hook.first_line: What is all this inventory? You spent your savings on clothes?

montage.description: Wordless, music-driven 'how the business works' grind montage (7.9 s, 14 shots): typing a listing, holding up a spider-web hoodie under camera-flash pops (product photos), resale-site listing screens with a finger tapping, phone in hand, a 'sold' pop-up, sealing the hoodie in a poly mailer with a shipping label, a thermal printer spitting a label, his face lit by a phone in the dark, then two locked-off frontal shots with day/night light flicker (time-lapse) as he wilts into his chair. Ends on exhaustion, which sets up the night 'still doing this?' scene.

stats.dead_air: None in the audio sense: a music bed runs the full 60 s (silencedetect at -35 dB/0.4 s found no silence). Gaps with no dialogue (>= 1.5 s): 11.52-20.35 (8.8 s), 24.01-26.75 (2.7 s), 30.25-36.30 (6.0 s), 39.35-47.85 (8.5 s), 49.65-52.20 (2.6 s), 57.08-59.84 (2.8 s).

beats.summary: HOOK: Mom bursts in, 'What is all this inventory? You spent your savings on clothes?' - 'I'm reselling them.' - 'How many have you sold?' - 'Two.'
Ultimatum: snap zoom into Mom's glare: 'Exactly. Take them back and focus on school.' Son: 'Just give me a month.' Mom unconvinced; dip to black.
MONTAGE: the grind - photograph, list, sell, pack, print labels; days pass in light flicker until he slumps in his chair.
Doubt at night: Mom in the lit doorway behind him: 'You're still doing this?' - 'Yeah, because I know I can make it work.' She leaves; sale notifications start popping up around him. 'Wait...'
Breakthrough: crash zoom to his eyes reflecting sale prices ($330 / $550): 'Yo...' then he leaps up: 'Yeah!'
Scale: locked-off time-lapse of him packing in fast motion while stacks grow; Mom appears in the doorway at normal speed: 'What happened?' - 'They're selling all of them. I'm trying...'
Grind 2 + Mom joins: day/night jump cuts of packing, he falls asleep face-down on a hoodie; Mom walks in: 'What are you doing? You're doing it wrong.' and starts packing with him.
Button: high five, 'Told ya.' - 'Don't get cocky.' The closet door behind them swings open on a wall of new boxes. 'You bought more?' - 'Huh... maybe.' Whip to Mom's horrified ECU.
Real-me tag: 11 rapid handheld lifestyle clips (stock room, yacht, friends and cars, Rolls-Royce, sunset jet ski, dinner by the marina, designer shopping bags, starlight car interior).

transcription: faster-whisper 'small' (CPU, int8), word timestamps; dialogue windows re-run one by one (no VAD) and cross-checked against the burned-in word captions. 'Yeah!' and 'Huh' come from captions only; 'Yo', 'Don't get cocky', 'You bought more? ... maybe' were missed by the first pass and recovered on the re-run.
why_it_works: The hook is a named doubter: the title card 'MOM SAID I'D FAIL' plus Mom bursting through the door makes the whole reel a 'prove her wrong' promise in the first second.
The opening joke-answer ('How many have you sold?' - 'Two.') lands the stakes and the humiliation in one word, then a snap zoom into Mom's glare doubles it.
Big, readable face acting (saucer eyes, gritted teeth, slow jaw drops) carries each beat on mute; captions are one word at a time so the eye stays on faces.
The grind montage teaches the actual business (photo, list, sell, pack, print label) in 8 s with no words - it doubles as content for the reselling audience the CTA targets.
Time passes through light, not titles: day/night flicker on locked-off frames and fast-motion packing with Mom at normal speed show weeks in seconds.
The breakthrough is a single visual gag - sale prices reflected in his eyes - followed by a full-body jump; the payoff is physical, not explained.
Mom's arc flips from opponent to partner ('You're doing it wrong' while packing next to him) - a warmer payoff than revenge, and very shareable with parents.
The button is a comic reversal (closet of new boxes, 'You bought more?' - 'maybe') ending on a horror ECU, so the reel ends on a laugh, not a lecture.
The live-action tag links the cartoon to a real lifestyle ('based on a true story' caption) and the fast cuts invite a loop/rewatch.
undetermined: Music identity not identified (music bed under everything; only speech transcribed).
Speakers of 'Two.', 'Told ya.', 'Don't get cocky.' and 'Huh... maybe.' inferred from mouth movement and context, not certain.
'Yeah!' (29.65 s) and 'Huh' (56.2 s) are from captions only; their timings follow the captions.
Shot 24 (9.9 s) is treated as one locked-off time-lapse shot: framing never changes, but fast-motion ghosting may hide speed-ramp joins.
Shots 25-28 are counted as separate shots (hard day/night jump cuts on the same set-up); shot 19 and 20 light flicker on one set-up is counted as one shot each.
Shot 30's fast push at 53.9 s (door swings open, camera pushes to a profile two-shot) is counted as one continuous move, not a cut.
Tag shot count (11) is from frame differences plus a 0.05 s strip; very short handheld whips may merge two clips.
Screen inserts (shots 9, 12, 15) change page content inside the shot; treated as one shot each.
